old_description: Stable electricity is one of the most recurrent problems of rural areas. At Universal Solar, LLC, we want to help our customers to enjoy power even when there are blackouts. We’re a solar company serving in Millersburg, PA, with almost a decade of experience in the industry. We take pride in providing our customers with energy-efficient solutions for their properties. If you’re looking for a trusted solar company in Millersburg, PA, you’re in the right place!
about:
Universal Solar, LLC is based in Millersburg, Pennsylvania. The company has been operating for nearly a decade, though a specific founding year is not disclosed. It began as a response to unstable electricity in rural areas, aiming to provide energy-efficient solutions for properties in the region.

The company provides solar energy system design, installation, repair, and maintenance. Services include off-grid solar systems, grid-tied systems, grid-interactive systems, roof-mounted and ground-mount solar panel installations, battery storage solutions, and solar water pumping (Simple Pump). They serve residential, commercial, and industrial clients. No facility size, headcount, or volume metrics are published.

Universal Solar serves homeowners, businesses, and industrial facilities across central and northeastern Pennsylvania, including Millersburg, Bloomsburg, Lewisburg, Williamsport, Scranton, and Wilkes-Barre. Customers range from residential property owners seeking backup power to commercial and industrial operations looking to lower energy costs.

The company emphasizes energy independence and reliability during grid outages, positioning its installations as a way to avoid peak-rate charges and reduce environmental impact. Financing options are offered to lower the upfront investment barrier.

name: Uptown Millworks
old_description: Uptown Millworks is a New Orleans millwork shop and furniture maker specializing in quality, style and function. We work to make a comfortable, personal environment from every client's needs. The finishing touch of beauty and personality for any room.
about:
Uptown Millworks operates from its workshop in New Orleans, Louisiana. Founded by Christian Pokorn, a woodworker from a multi-generational Austrian sawmill family who also leads Pokorn Construction, the shop began as a locally owned and operated custom millwork business dedicated to the architectural heritage of its home city.

The company produces architectural millwork, casework, and furniture using time-tested woodworking techniques alongside modern precision tools. Services span handrails, flooring, cypress slabs, custom cabinets, moldings, windows, doors, shutters, and turnings. A team of millwrights, carpenters, and woodworkers executes each project from the New Orleans facility, sourcing, manufacturing, and finishing all work on-site without maintaining large inventory.

Uptown Millworks serves residential, hospitality, and commercial clients across Louisiana, including historic homes, restaurants, hotels, and upscale buildings in the greater New Orleans area. The shop frequently collaborates on historically faithful restorations guided by the New Orleans Historic District Landmarks Commission.

The firm distinguishes itself through a commitment to local manufacturing, sustainable material sourcing (FSC-certified woods), and adherence to Architectural Woodwork Institute standards. Waste is minimized by repurposing offcuts for smaller details or donating to community gardens and shelters, and every piece is delivered and installed by the company's own crew.

name: Urth Apparel Inc.
old_description: Urth Apparel Inc. is a custom apparel manufacturer based in Newport Beach, California, that takes clothing brands from concept through production. Services include product development, fashion and technical design, fabric and trim sourcing, pattern making, grading, marker making, sampling, cutting and sewing, screen printing, sublimation, heat transfer, finishing, packaging and inspection. Production is split by origin: luxury clothing in Italy, knitwear and basics in Peru, and specialty technical apparel in the USA. about:
Urth Apparel Inc. is a custom apparel manufacturer headquartered in Newport Beach, California. The company was founded in 2013 when its founder launched an international trade cooperative focused on natural foods and cotton apparel from Peru. The venture grew from a desire to find manufacturing partners that shared a commitment to both fashionable design and ecological responsibility.

Urth Apparel manages the full product development cycle, including fashion and technical design, fabric and trim sourcing, pattern making, grading, marker making, sampling, cutting and sewing, screen printing, sublimation, heat transfer, finishing, packaging, and inspection. Production is distributed across three origins: luxury clothing in Italy, knitwear and basics in Peru, and specialty technical apparel in the United States. The company operates dedicated production lines for tees, tanks, and polos, and emphasizes sustainable and organic materials. The core team at headquarters numbers three employees.

Its portfolio spans tees, tanks, polos, dresses, kids and baby apparel, yoga and athleisure wear, swimwear, and dress shirts. Industries served include fashion apparel, sustainable and organic clothing, activewear, swimwear, and children’s wear.

The founders created Urth Apparel after struggling to find factories that combined quality, sustainability, and fair labor practices. The company’s stated philosophy is to “do it right, take care of the planet, take care of your workers, create clothing that lasts.” It positions itself as a one-stop partner that handles design, sourcing, and logistics, with daily communication between design teams and production floors.

The company buys and sells new, used, obsolete, and hard-to-find electrical equipment, with a focus on molded case circuit breakers, hardware kits, transformers, safety switches, bus plugs, MCC buckets, and starters. name: Utility Wire Products
old_description: Utility Wire Products, Inc. specializes in Point of Purchase Display Racks. We can produce a rack from your design, or work with you to develop a design, anything from a single display rack to meet a one product display need or a whole group to fill up a Plan-O-Gram for your product line.
about:
Utility Wire Products, Inc. operates from a 48,000-square-foot facility on Cleveland’s industrial East Side at 3302 East 87th Street. The company was founded in 1953 by Ed Peck and Bill Milavac. Donald Anzells acquired the business in 1980, and it remains family-owned and trans-generational; current president Ronald Anzells has been with the firm for 30 years, joined by his son Ronald Anzells Jr. as plant manager and custom tooling designer in 2007.

The shop specializes in custom wire products across five major lines: point-of-purchase display racks, wire guards for lighting, fans, machinery and heaters, wire baskets, custom wire forms, and grid assemblies. Wire diameters range from .080 to .500 inch, worked in bright basic, stainless steel, and galvanized wire, with tubing, sheet metal, and plastics incorporated as needed. An on-site 3D CNC bending machine handles forming, and finishing options include powder coating, vinyl, nylon, and various plating processes. The company states it can run orders from a single unit up to 500,000 pieces.

Customers span retail merchandising (plan-o-gram display racks), industrial safety (guards for lights, fans, and high-temperature equipment), healthcare (baskets for hospital stretchers), and general manufacturing (containers for screw-machine parts). The firm works from customer designs or develops designs collaboratively.

The company’s stated motto is to deliver a ‘Quality Product in a Timely Fashion at a Fair Price that are American made,’ and its philosophy emphasizes treating every order—whether one piece or half a million—with equal importance and personal attention.

name: V-Tron Electronics Corporation
old_description: Manufacturers of High-Quality Assemblies, Wire Harnesses, Box Build, and Fiber Optic Assemblies
about:
V-Tron Electronics Corporation operates from a 45,000-square-foot facility in Attleboro, Massachusetts. The company was incorporated in 1970 as a privately held, veteran-owned small business, initially serving the emerging Massachusetts computer industry before expanding into semiconductors, medical, military, and industrial electronics.

The company provides electronic manufacturing services including cable assemblies, wire harnesses, fiber optic assemblies, molded connector assemblies, and box build assemblies. Its process engineering team performs pre-production manufacturability analysis and reverse engineering to create documented, repeatable manufacturing roadmaps. Production is managed through a real-time, bar-coded ERP system that tracks jobs from order inception to final inspection, supporting low-to-high volume order lot sizes.

V-Tron serves defense and security, medical and life sciences, semiconductor, and industrial electronics customers. Its assemblies are built to IPC standards and tested 100 percent using Cirris 4250 scanners for cable and harness continuity, while fiber optic links are verified for insertion loss and visual defects. The company holds UL and cUL recognition for wiring harnesses (E76510) and power supply cords (E173242), plus CSA certification (LR56498-1).

President Doug Gobin emphasizes that quality and reliability are keys to survival, a philosophy reflected in an in-house training program certified to IPC-A-610, IPC/WHMA-A-620, and J-STD-001. The firm’s quality system is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and focuses on continuous improvement, on-time delivery, and scrap reduction.

old_description: Vip Rubber and Plastic is one of the best rubber and plastic manufacturing facilities in America. We specialize in custom rubber extrusions, plastic extrusions, rubber sheet products, molded rubber products, plastic pipe and tubing. We have been manufacturing high-quality parts in the USA since 1961.
about:
VIP Rubber and Plastic operates from Minden, Nevada, where it has been manufacturing rubber and plastic products since 1961. The company was founded by Howard Vipperman Sr., known as “Big Vip,” who entered the rubber industry as a gasket cutter after serving in the armed forces. It remains a family-owned American manufacturer now led by subsequent generations.

The company specializes in custom rubber extrusions, plastic extrusions, rubber sheet and roll products, molded rubber parts, and plastic pipe and tubing. It also offers custom rubber compounding and a suite of value-added fabrication services under its Vip+ Services program, positioning itself as a one-stop shop. Production includes solid rod, cord, profiles, seals, gaskets, window and door seals, and vinyl spline.

VIP serves a range of industries including aerospace, agriculture, automotive, architectural glass and metal, and construction. Its facility is an approved manufacturer for several Boeing material specifications and holds AS9100 certification, supplying top aerospace organizations. The company also produces parts for custom applications across virtually every industry.

The company emphasizes its family-owned heritage, generations of manufacturing experience, and the integration of Excalibur Extrusions’ plastic extrusion capabilities. It highlights its AS9100-certified quality system, ITAR registration, and the fact that all products are manufactured in the USA as key differentiators.

name: VMS - Fulfillment, Assembly and Warehousing
old_description: Our mission here at VMS Inc., a 3PL and fulfillment provider, is to seamlessly connect businesses with tailored, efficient, and innovative service solutions. Through cutting-edge technology, unparalleled expertise, and a commitment to excellence, we aim to optimize supply chains, streamline operations, and enhance customer service and satisfaction. Together, we navigate challenges, deliver reliability, and create lasting partnerships that drive growth and success for our clients in an ever-evolving marketplace.
about:
VMS operates from a 12,000-square-foot facility in West Rutland, Vermont, conveniently located near major transportation routes to New York, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Maine, and Canada. The business has more than three decades of industry experience and was acquired by Jessica Dambrackas in 2011 when she purchased the former Rutland Industries, continuing a legacy of contract manufacturing, fulfillment, and packaging services.

The company provides a range of outsourced services including quality control, distribution, inventory management, kitting, packaging, assembly, pick-and-pack, e-commerce fulfillment, warehousing, and cross-docking. Its climate-controlled warehouse and loading docks accommodate various truck sizes, while specialized software integrates with e-commerce shopping carts for rapid order processing. The team handles everything from basic hand assembly to comprehensive offsite manufacturing and packaging divisions, operating under lean manufacturing principles.

VMS serves clients across diverse sectors such as electronics manufacturing, food packaging, e-commerce, fashion, and publishing. Notable customers have included the Rutland Herald for bundle distribution and startup companies requiring flexible warehousing and accurate order fulfillment. The company's clientele spans both large and small businesses seeking to reduce overhead and streamline supply chains.

A core differentiator is the company's social mission: Dambrackas established VMS to employ as many individuals with disabilities as possible, a commitment that guided the acquisition and remains central to operations. The firm also emphasizes fixed pricing to simplify expense forecasting and aims to lower clients' costs associated with advertising, training, payroll taxes, and benefits. This community-focused approach, combined with over 30 years of operational experience, positions VMS as a partner for businesses seeking reliable, cost-effective outsourcing.

about:
Valley Woodcraft & Lumber Co operates from Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, where it was founded in 1952.

The shop produces custom wood, phenolic, composite, and machined-plastic components and assembled products from customer prints. Its process capabilities include CAD/CAM design, CNC nested-based machining, drilling, finishing, profiling, sanding, shaping, mortise-and-tenon joinery, laminating, gluing, fingerjointing, paraffin treatment of lumber, and both commercial and mil-spec packaging. The facility handles everything from simple dimensional stock to complex assemblies, with a product portfolio that spans cable cleats, clamps, wedges, blocks, spacers, wheel chocks, floor panels, ladders, and hundreds of other precision parts.

Valley Woodcraft serves aerospace, defense, rail, transit, construction, maritime, furniture, and utility industries. Its AS9100 and ISO 9001 certifications cover the manufacture of high-precision machined parts for aviation, aerospace, transportation, and defense customers. Representative parts include cable fairleads, burnout sticks, switch wedges, phenolic pads, tunnel insulation, and structural components such as floor beams and bulkhead protectors.

The company emphasizes assured product quality, competitive pricing, on-time delivery, and the flexibility to fulfill any order size. Its veteran-owned status and dedicated team with advanced technology are cited as key differentiators, along with a commitment to superior customer service that has been maintained since 1952.

name: Valley Woodworkers
old_description: The Valley Woodworkers of West Virginia cares about our community and does what we can to improve it.  The mission of the Valley Woodworkers of West Virginia is twofold.  One part is the training of local community members to be woodworker. Whether it be honing their craft to later become a professional woodworker, or merely to create handcrafted heirloom pieces for their friends and family.  Secondly, since 1991, the Valley Woodworkers have been making heirloom quality wooden toys for the Salvation Army to distribute to underprivileged children at Christmas.
about:
Valley Woodworkers operates from Dunbar, West Virginia. The organization traces its roots to 1991 when members began crafting heirloom wooden toys for the Salvation Army’s Christmas distribution. The club was formally established in 2008 as a gathering point for woodworkers of all skill levels. It is a community-focused group supported by local sponsors such as Woodcraft and Withrow Supply.

The club’s activities center on woodworking education and charitable production. Members meet monthly at the clubhouse on 12th Street for show-and-tell sessions and demonstrations covering techniques such as dovetail joinery, band-saw box making, and cradle building. Since 1991, the group has produced wooden toys for underprivileged children at Christmas.

Valley Woodworkers serves the local woodworking community—beginners, amateurs, and professionals—along with the Salvation Army as a charitable recipient. Sponsors include Woodcraft and Withrow Supply, which provide machinery, hardware, and finishing supplies. The club also partners with Clonch Industries, Inc., though the nature of the relationship is not detailed.

The organization’s stated mission is twofold: to train community members in woodworking, whether for professional development or personal fulfillment, and to continue the tradition of donating handcrafted toys to children in need.

about:
Valley Woodworks LLC was founded in 2022 by Jonathan Dias in Palmer, Massachusetts. Dias, a graduate of Springfield College with a degree in Business Administration and a minor in Entrepreneurial Studies, started the company after deciding he could not spend his career in an office. He began building furniture by hand with the goal of creating pieces that lacked the commercial, mass-produced feel of typical retail offerings.

The workshop produces custom tables and furniture on a commission basis. Each piece starts as a solid hardwood slab, hand-selected for grain, moisture content, and character. The company uses no veneers, plywood cores, or engineered composites. Finishes are hand-rubbed hardwax oils that protect the wood while leaving the grain visible and pores open.

Valley Woodworks serves residential clients seeking heirloom-quality furniture for their homes. Customers engage directly with the maker through a design consultation, resulting in one-of-a-kind dining tables, desks, and other pieces intended to anchor a living space for generations. The company does not sell through retailers or maintain inventory; every item is made to order.

Dias founded the business to counter what he describes as a click-to-buy culture that prioritizes speed over longevity. The stated mission is to keep the art of fine furniture making alive by delivering pieces that are passed down rather than replaced. The company’s differentiator is its commitment to solid-wood construction and transparent finishing that shows the material’s natural character.

name: Vermont Electric Power Company
old_description: VELCO is the owner/operator of Vermont’s high-voltage transmission system and does not directly serve individual homes and businesses. We deliver the power to your local distribution company which then delivers it to you.
about:
Vermont Electric Power Company (VELCO), headquartered in Rutland, Vermont, was created in 1956 as the nation's first statewide, transmission-only electric utility. The company was formed to build and operate an interconnected high-voltage transmission grid that would deliver and share access to clean power, including hydroelectric resources, across Vermont. Ownership is held by the state's 17 distribution utilities and a public benefits corporation, and its for-profit structure is designed to return value to those owners, their customers, and all Vermonters.

VELCO owns and operates the high-voltage transmission system that moves electricity from generation sources to local distribution companies, which then serve homes and businesses. The company does not directly serve retail customers. Its work encompasses transmission system planning, grid reliability management, and the interconnection of generation resources. VELCO also publishes an annual ESG report and maintains a safety culture focused on employee well-being.

The primary customers are Vermont's 17 distribution utilities, including municipal departments such as Burlington Electric Department, Stowe Electric Department, and others listed as owners. Through these utilities, VELCO's transmission network ultimately serves residential, commercial, and industrial end-users across the state. The company also engages with regional energy stakeholders to provide a unified voice on transmission and clean energy issues.

VELCO distinguishes itself as the first transmission-only company of its kind in the United States, a model that remains unique. Its ownership structure and mandate to return value to utility owners and ratepayers set it apart from investor-owned utilities. The company emphasizes environmental stewardship, sustainability initiatives, and a commitment to a reliable, affordable, and secure grid as core differentiators.

about:
Virginia Food Works operates a VDACS-inspected commercial kitchen at the Prince Edward County Cannery in Farmville, Virginia. The nonprofit organization was established to support Virginia farmers by offering a rental production facility for small-batch commercial retail co-packing during harvest season.

The facility provides access to licensed equipment including kettles, mixers, fillers, and canners for hot-fill, water-bath, and pressure canning processes. Commercial clients schedule appointments Thursday through Saturday, with reservations recommended up to a month ahead during the peak season from June through December. The shared-use model allows growers to process seasonal harvests such as tomatoes, berries, apples, peppers, and ginger root into shelf-stable acid and acidified products.

Services are directed at Virginia and out-of-state farmers as well as emerging small-business food entrepreneurs. The cannery produces sauces, jams, relishes, syrups, and similar value-added items, but cannot handle meat, fish, or dairy due to licensing scope. Clients receive guidance on recipe scaling, regulatory compliance including Process Authority Review and VDACS registration, and food safety training such as ServSafe and Better Process Control School.

The organization’s stated mission is to strengthen Virginia’s food system by reducing waste, preserving crops, and expanding market opportunities for local producers through value-added production. A resource-first approach aims to equip clients with knowledge of cost structures, scheduling, and regulatory requirements before they commit to commercial runs.

The company serves individual clients seeking one-of-a-kind furnishings, as well as restoration projects for Victorian-era homes. Past work includes custom chess tables, toy vehicles, charcuterie boards, jewelry boxes, and period-appropriate millwork for historic renovations.

Carlough’s background in teaching and historic renovation informs a focus on designing and constructing each piece to the customer’s exact wishes, emphasizing heirloom quality and traditional joinery.

name: WORLD electronics
old_description: WORLD electronics is a flexible, customer focused manufacturer of printed circuit board assemblies of various volumes, mixes and complexities.
about:
WORLD electronics operates from Reading, Pennsylvania, where the company has been based since 1999. The business traces its roots to 1991, and in 1986 Joe Rado purchased the company, moving it from West Chester to Morgantown before designing the current Reading facility. Under Rado's leadership the firm grew from eight people to over 100 employees. Since 2018 the Rado family's women have led the company, which holds WBENC certification as a woman-owned business.

The company provides turnkey printed circuit board assembly and box-build services for low-to-medium-volume, high-mix production. Its shop runs six independent surface-mount lines, through-hole soldering, a Kulicke & Soffa 8090 wedge wire bonder, automated optical inspection, X-ray inspection, in-circuit and functional test, burn-in and temperature cycling, component programming, rework, cleaning and pin insertion. Engineering support covers design for manufacturability, test development, PCB layout and supply-chain management.

Customers span communications, networking, medical, defense and industrial-control sectors, ranging from major OEMs to high-tech start-ups. The firm handles both tin-lead and RoHS-compliant assemblies, offering surface finishes such as HASL, nickel-gold, OSP and immersion silver.

Joe Rado's motto — “We do things other people don't want to do” — still drives the culture. A flexible floor layout enables quick setup and teardown for prototype runs, while an integrated bar-coded ERP system provides real-time job tracking. The company emphasizes a supportive workplace and a “have some fun” attitude.

about:
Wei Chuan USA was founded in 1972 in Los Angeles by brothers Thomas and Robert Huang, recent immigrants from Taiwan who missed the authentic flavors of home. The company opened its first plant in Los Angeles in 1975 and expanded with a second facility in Tennessee in 2006. In 2018, the corporate headquarters moved to City of Industry, California, while the Tennessee plant remains a key production site.

The company manufactures a wide range of Chinese food products including gyoza, potstickers, spring rolls, egg rolls, buns, dumplings, wontons, wrappers, entrées, shumai, and a natural, organic, and vegetarian line. Production takes place in two USDA Grant of Inspection establishments that are also FDA-approved, operating under certified HACCP, GMP, and SSOP programs. An in-house R&D team of food scientists, nutritionists, and chefs develops and tests new recipes, balancing traditional flavors with modern convenience.

Wei Chuan USA serves both retail grocery channels and food‑service operators across the United States. Its products are distributed through a network of branch offices in California, Texas, New Jersey, Illinois, and Georgia, reaching supermarkets, Asian specialty stores, and restaurant distributors. The company also supplies a dedicated food‑service category for bulk and institutional use.

The founders started the business because they believed food is a cultural bridge that connects people to their roots. The company’s stated mission is to be the provider of high‑quality Chinese food products in the U.S., upholding tradition while embracing innovation to make authentic flavors convenient for everyone.

about:
The West Tennessee Solar Exhibit is located in Stanton, Tennessee. The project originated from a $62.5-million allocation of federal American Recovery and Reinvestment Act funds to the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development in 2009. The department contracted with the University of Tennessee to oversee the creation and operation of the solar farm through the UT Research Foundation. Signal Energy, LLC of Chattanooga designed and built the array in 2011, with grid connection achieved in early 2012.

The facility spans more than 25 acres and houses approximately 21,000 fixed-tilt, ground-mounted photovoltaic panels. Electricity generated is sold under purchase agreements with Chickasaw Electric Cooperative and the Tennessee Valley Authority. In addition to power production, the site hosts SPECTRUM, an educational exhibit that walks visitors through the history, current technology, and future of solar energy in Tennessee through interactive displays and games.

The operation serves the advanced energy and renewable energy sectors, with direct utility customers including Chickasaw Electric Cooperative and TVA. Partners in the effort include Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council, the Tennessee Renewable Energy & Economic Development Council, and multiple state agencies.

The initiative was launched under the Volunteer State Solar Initiative, a comprehensive program focused on job creation, education, renewable power production, and technology commercialization. The exhibit aims to connect visitors with practical solar applications and inspire the next generation of energy professionals.

The firm's ISO 13485:2016 certification supports regulated programs requiring contamination control, DNA-free molding, and full validation documentation.

Rooted in toolmaking, Westec differentiates itself by combining in-house tool design and fabrication with a flexible sourcing strategy that leverages domestic and offshore partners. The company emphasizes process control through statistical process control, first article inspection, and real-time production monitoring, aiming to reduce supply chain risk while maintaining tight tolerances and consistent quality from prototype through full-scale production.

Westinghouse Electric Co LLC, headquartered in Hopkins, South Carolina, traces its origins to 1869 when George Westinghouse founded Westinghouse Electric Company. The enterprise began with innovations in rail travel and electric power, later extending into nuclear energy in 1957 with the world's first commercial pressurized water reactor.

Today the company designs and manufactures nuclear reactors, fuel, and components, supplying over 100,000 nuclear parts annually. Its technology powers 57 percent of the world's nuclear power plants, maintains nearly two-thirds of the global fleet, and fuels 40 percent of that fleet. With approximately 12,500 employees across more than 100 locations in 23 countries, Westinghouse provides integrated services for routine maintenance, emergent issues, and new plant deployment, including the AP1000 Generation III+ reactor with passive safety features.

The company serves utilities and nuclear operators worldwide. Recent customers include Polish suppliers for the first AP1000 unit at Lubiatowo-Kopalino, the Ringhals plant in Sweden for clevis bolt replacement, and the ITER project in Europe for vacuum vessel sectors. Its services span operating plant support, new plant construction, and innovation programs such as the PWROG AI Assistant.

Westinghouse positions itself as an indispensable partner for global nuclear expansion, stating that the world cannot meet energy demands without nuclear and cannot build more nuclear without Westinghouse. Its differentiation rests on a legacy of first-of-a-kind technology, industrial scale, and a vision to shape the next generation of nuclear innovation.

White Bag serves agricultural and industrial packaging markets, with memberships in the Flexible Intermediate Bulk Container Association, the Southern Seed Association, and the Textile Bag and Packaging Association.

The company emphasizes its founder's original commitment to product quality and customer service as its guiding principle, supplemented by a strategy of maintaining ready stock through global sourcing and offering on-site printing to shorten lead times.

Wisconsin Metal Parts operates from Waukesha, Wisconsin. The company was founded in 1988 as Die Concepts, Inc., and spent its first 22 years building a tool-and-die business while listening to customer needs. Customers span aerospace, agriculture, foodservice, medical, and defense sectors. The company has produced military ordnance components such as mechanical fuzes, high-volume progressive die stampings for the container industry, and assemblies ranging from cabinets to clamping fixtures. It also supports commercial and industrial clients nationwide.

Wisconsin Metal Parts emphasizes intellectual value and a “Golden Rule” culture—treating customers, employees, and suppliers with respect. Its cross-trained workforce moves between departments to maintain workflow, and in-house tooling capabilities allow it to take over existing stamping dies and manage complex, multi-process parts from prototype through assembly.

about:
Wise Plastics Technologies traces its roots to 1974, when it was founded as Wise‑Hamlin Plastics in the greater Chicagoland area. Today the company is headquartered in St. Charles, Illinois, with additional facilities in West Chicago, placing it roughly 30 minutes from downtown Chicago and O’Hare International Airport.

The molder operates more than 100 injection presses ranging from 35 to 1,100 tons across three purpose‑built plants totaling over 350,000 square feet. Core processes include precision plastic injection molding, two‑shot, insert and over‑molding, liquid silicone rubber (LSR) molding for medical‑grade and biocompatible applications, and scientific molding supported by RJG‑certified decoupled processes and automation on every cell. Value‑added services span assembly, sonic welding, heat staking, decorating, packaging, kitting, and full contract‑manufacturing programs that cover tooling transfers, design‑for‑manufacturing, supply‑chain management, and just‑in‑time delivery. A staff of 200+ runs production 24/5, shifting to 24/7 when demand requires.

The company serves medical device and pharmaceutical customers with ISO 13485:2016‑certified quality systems and clean‑room LSR capability, defense programs under ITAR registration, and a broad range of industrial OEMs that rely on its integrated supply‑chain and logistics support.

Wise Plastics emphasizes five decades of manufacturing discipline, modern equipment, and a quality‑first culture codified in ISO 9001:2015 and OSHA SHARP certifications. Its stated differentiators include purpose‑built facilities, integrated operations, advanced automation, an experienced team, ultra‑responsive service, and a commitment to continuous improvement across quality, innovation, employee respect, integrity, and sustainability.

The founders' original vision — to craft timeless, quality, real wood products made in America and built to last — remains the stated mission. name: World Finer Foods, Inc.
old_description: Max H. Ries, a German immigrant who operated a textile firm in his native Munich, left Germany in 1939 and had intended to develop a similar company in Chicago. But when he arrived in the U.S., he believed he would be better off importing food. In 1947, he founded Reese Finer Foods, and its major brand “Reese” quickly became the leading brand of specialty foods in the U.S.
about:
World Finer Foods, Inc. is headquartered in Bloomfield, New Jersey. The company traces its roots to 1947 when German immigrant Max H. Ries founded Reese Finer Foods after arriving in the United States in 1939. Originally intending to establish a textile business in Chicago, Ries pivoted to importing specialty foods, and the Reese brand quickly became a name in the U.S. specialty food market.

Today, World Finer Foods manages and markets more than 1,000 owned and third‑party premium food, beverage, and personal‑care products across over 60 brands. The firm provides a full suite of services — sales and category management, trade and consumer marketing, finance (order processing, invoicing, promotional spend, deductions, collections), and logistics (EDI, FDA compliance, inventory control, warehousing) — all supported by an Oracle ERP platform. It acts as the exclusive U.S. customer for its brand partners, selling to more than 350 retail and distribution accounts.

The company serves brand owners in the specialty food, beverage, and personal‑care sectors, including both domestic and international producers. Its portfolio includes long‑standing brands such as Reese (the top‑selling U.S. brand for artichoke hearts, hearts of palm, and prepared horseradish), Kitchens of India, Barry’s Tea, Nando’s, DaVinci, and La Posada. Customers range from traditional grocery retailers and distributors to emerging e‑commerce channels.

World Finer Foods emphasizes relationship‑driven growth, a philosophy dating to its early partnerships with European brands like Panni, Knorr, and Maggi. It is the only U.S. member of the Circle of European Specialty Food Distributors (CEISA) and a member of the Specialty Food Association and The Food Institute. The firm’s comprehensive approach — combining sales, marketing, finance, and logistics under one roof — is designed to let brand owners focus on product development while World Finer Foods handles market access.

about:
Zero Manufacturing is headquartered in North Salt Lake, Utah, and traces its founding to 1931 when German immigrant Herman Zierold established a sheet-metal shop in Los Angeles after crafting a rugged aluminum case to protect his engineering documents in the California oil fields. The business evolved through several ownership changes and was acquired by private equity firm Rockwood Equity Partners, with Declan Mclaughlin serving as CEO.

The company designs and manufactures protective cases and enclosures for mission-critical equipment, working in both aluminum and plastic. Its 286,000-square-foot facility employs 145 people and runs processes that include deep-drawn aluminum forming, rotomolding, laser cutting, Trumpf TruPunch pressing, certified welding, anodizing, powder coating, and custom assembly. Annual output exceeds 270,000 parts across more than 2,600 unique SKUs for a customer base of over 3,100 accounts.

Zero serves aerospace, defense, military, medical, energy, oil and gas, industrial, electronics and infrastructure, and logistics sectors. Its cases have protected avionics and flight hardware, medical diagnostics and life-saving devices, downhole sensors in harsh oilfield environments, and notably the Apollo 11 moon rock containers.

The company was born from a need to shield valuable documents from extreme field conditions, and it states its purpose is to help teams protect what matters through disciplined engineering, controlled domestic manufacturing, and long-term partnership. It emphasizes a fully U.S.-based, vertically integrated production model and an engineering-led approach that includes design guidance at no cost.

The company serves food brands and entrepreneurs across the frozen, gluten-free, allergen-free, and plant-based segments. Clients range from startups launching vegan cheese and butter spreads to established brands needing co-packing for IQF produce, ready-to-eat meals, and variety packs. ZoRoCo's dedicated gluten-free plant (built 2022) and Big 9 allergen-free capabilities allow it to handle sensitive formulations without cross-contamination risk.

ZoRoCo positions itself as a non-competitor—it markets no brands of its own—and emphasizes transparency through live client access to production, inventory, and shipping data. The founders cite an entrepreneurial mentality, precision execution, and certification and claims management as core differentiators, aiming to protect clients' intellectual property while scaling capacity alongside their growth.

about:
iSolar is based in St. Paul Park, Minnesota, and was co-founded in 2019 by master electrician John Ihle and his nephew Ryan Ihle. The company is family-owned and veteran-owned, with roots in the Minnesota electrical trade dating back to 1977 and renewable-energy work since the 1980s — experience the firm says few other solar installers in the state can match.

iSolar provides full-service solar, storage, and electrical work for homes, farms, and businesses across Minnesota. Its services cover residential solar, commercial and agricultural solar, battery backup, EV charger installation, electrical panel upgrades, wiring, standby generators, and solar array detach-and-reset for roofing projects. The company uses its own crew for installations, completing most residential jobs in one to two days under master electrician license EA761814. It holds manufacturer certifications for major brands including Enphase, SolarEdge, Tesla Powerwall, Generac, and Kohler, and backs every system with a 30-year insurance-backed warranty through Solar Insure plus a 20-year battery warranty.

The installer serves Minnesota homeowners, farmers, businesses, schools, and public entities. Since 2020 it has helped income-qualified families access solar at little-to-no cost through Xcel Energy's Solar*Rewards Income-Qualified program. Since 2019 it has assisted farmers with projects funded partly by USDA REAP grants. Public-sector work includes solar on school buildings and a 100 kW AC array at Edina City Hall. iSolar has also been selected as a co-op installer by Solar United Neighbors for 2022, 2023, and 2024.

The company says it was started to do solar "the right way" for neighbors — emphasizing a single local crew from start to finish with no subcontractor shuffle, custom solutions from experienced designers, honest fair pricing, and a 30-year warranty. Its family-owned, veteran-owned structure and deep Minnesota roots are presented as reasons customers can trust the firm for the long term.

The company designs and manufactures industrial control panels, pushbutton stations, cable assemblies, and wire harnesses. Capabilities span motor control centers, relay-based and PLC panels, HMI panels, wall-mounted and cable-drop pushbutton stations, and cable assemblies using NEMA, pin-and-sleeve, military, data, ribbon, and coaxial connectors. The firm handles both high and low volumes — from a single Type 1 pushbutton station to runs of 1,000 UL 508A panels — and reports shipping millions of wire harnesses globally each year.

Customers come from industrial automation, automotive, military and defense, and data communications sectors. The company works with OEMs and other buyers who need custom panels, harnesses, or cable assemblies built to print, and it can incorporate customer-supplied parts or leverage its own OEM contract pricing.

A.B. Electrical Wires emphasizes personal service and turnkey delivery. It stocks standard multi-conductor cable for quick turnaround, offers 100 percent testing with documentation, and positions its employee-ownership model as a driver of accountability and responsiveness.

The SuperMold program differentiates ASH by delivering steel tooling and first articles in as little as 10 days for $4,900, replacing traditional short-life prototype tooling. Combined with ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 13485:2016 certification, ITAR registration, and a fully integrated in-house workflow, the company positions itself for complex, tight-tolerance projects that demand speed and regulatory compliance.

about:

Today Accu-Mold operates a 9,000‑square‑foot facility that was rebuilt after an F‑1 tornado destroyed the original plant in 2006. The shop houses automated injection molding machines ranging from 22 to 125 tons of clamping force, with shot capacities from 1.2 to just under 9 ounces. In‑house capabilities include mold design using SOLIDWORKS, Mastercam and AutoCAD, CNC machining, sinker EDM, surface grinding, manual machining and heat treating. A geothermal‑controlled clean room supports medical‑grade production, and the company offers overmolding, insert molding, assembly, packaging and just‑in‑time delivery.

The company serves the electronics and medical device sectors, with a historical focus on medical disposables. Its customer base includes both established manufacturers and start‑ups that rely on Accu‑Mold’s ability to move from single‑cavity prototypes to full‑scale production runs.

Accu‑Mold emphasizes efficiency, competitive pricing and responsive customer support as its core differentiators. By integrating the latest molding technologies with streamlined processes, the company aims to deliver high‑quality, precision components that help customers stay competitive, whether they need low‑volume prototypes or large production quantities.

about:
Roskam Foods, operating as Advanced Food Technologies, is headquartered in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Founded in 1923, the company began as a single-product operation and has grown into one of the largest multi-category external food manufacturers in the United States, backed by investor-led expansion.

The company provides co-manufacturing services for branded food companies, retailers, and private-label partners across snack foods, confections, frozen meals, pizza dough, dry baking mixes, and cereal and granola. Its processing platforms include twin- and single-screw extrusion, end-to-end bakery processing (mixing, sheeting, proofing, baking, tempering), specialty snack processing (drying, seasoning, air popping), and advanced packaging (stand-up pouches, dual-compartment cups, bag-in-box, bulk super-sacks). In-house engineering handles feasibility studies, line design, and turnkey capital project management. Operations span eight facilities in the U.S. and Canada, totaling over two million square feet of manufacturing and warehouse space, with more than 50 production and packaging lines and a workforce of 2,400-plus employees.

Customers include national retailers, high-growth brands, and private-label programs seeking large-scale, flexible production. Roskam serves categories such as better-for-you, organic, non-GMO, gluten-free, and grain-free formulations, with dedicated peanut-free facilities and controlled allergen handling for peanuts and tree nuts. The company also supports store-brand programs at national-brand quality.

Roskam emphasizes a partner-first mindset built on disciplined execution, continuous improvement, and integrated supply-chain support. Its differentiation rests on SQF Level II and III certification across all sites, in-house R&D from ideation through commercialization, and end-to-end logistics with EDI connectivity, enabling brands to consolidate manufacturing and simplify operations.
